name: options
label: Simulation Options
toolTip: Top-level container for all simulation configuration options.

fields.name: Simulation
fields.label: General simulation options
fields.toolTip: General options controlling how the simulation is carried out.

fields.name: simulation_type
fields.label: Simulation Type
valueDescriptions: Simulate full damage cascades, follow recoils
Simulate only ions, do not follow recoils
Simulate recoil cascades
fields.toolTip: Define the type of simulation.

fields.name: screening_type
fields.label: Screening Type
valueDescriptions: Unscreened Coulomb potential
Bohr screening
Kr-C screening
Moliere screening
Ziegler-Biersack-Littmark universal screening
ZBL with analytic approx. formula
fields.toolTip: Define the type of screening potential.
whatsThis: For Unscreened Coulomb and ZBL_MAGIC the scattering is calculated analytically.
In all other cases interpolation tables are used.

fields.name: electronic_stopping
fields.label: Electronic Stopping
valueDescriptions: No electronic stopping
Using the SRIM parametrization, v. 1996
Using the SRIM parametrization, v. 2013
Using the DPASS parametrization, v. 21.06
fields.toolTip: Calculation of electronic stopping.

fields.name: electronic_straggling
fields.label: Electronic Straggling
valueDescriptions: No electronic straggling.
According to the Bohr model
According to the model of Chu et al.
According to the model of Yang et al.
fields.toolTip: Calculation of electronic straggling.

fields.name: nrt_calculation
fields.label: NRT calculation
valueDescriptions: NRT calculated per recoil atom
NRT calculated using material average values
fields.toolTip: Define how to implement NRT in multielemental targets.
whatsThis: Material average Ed is calculated as 1/Ed = Σi{Xi / Edi} according to Ghoniem & Chou JNM1988

fields.name: intra_cascade_recombination
fields.label: Intra-cascade recombination
fields.toolTip: Enable intra-cascade recombination of Frenkel pairs.
whatsThis: When this option is enabled the Frenkel pairs within a PKA cascade may recombine under certain conditions.
Moving ions with E < Er can recombine with vacancies if their mutual distance R is below the recombination radius Rc (defined in the Target options for each atomic species).
The ion must be of the same atomic type as the one that was originally in the vacant site.

fields.name: time_ordered_cascades
fields.label: Time ordered recombinations in cascades [Experimental]
fields.toolTip: Time ordered recombinations in cascades [Experimental]

fields.name: correlated_recombination
fields.label: Allow same Frenkel pair recombination [Experimental]
fields.toolTip: Allow same Frenkel pair recombination [Experimental]

fields.name: move_recoil
fields.label: Move recoil atom to Rc [Experimental]
fields.toolTip: Move recoil atom to Rc [Experimental]

fields.name: recoil_sub_ed
fields.label: Subtract Ed from recoil energy [Experimental]
fields.toolTip: Subtract Ed from recoil energy [Experimental]

fields.name: Transport
fields.label: Ion transport options
fields.toolTip: Options controlling the transport of simulated ions, such as flight path sampling and energy cutoffs.

fields.name: min_energy
fields.label: Energy cutoff (eV)
fields.toolTip: Lowest kinetic energy of a simulated ion.
whatsThis: When the energy of an ion goes below this cutoff, the ion history is terminated.

fields.name: flight_path_type
fields.label: Flight Path Type
valueDescriptions: User-defined constant flight path
Sampled flight path, energy-dependent mean free path
fields.toolTip: Flight path sampling algorithm.

fields.name: flight_path_const
fields.label: Const. Flight Path (Rat)
fields.toolTip: Constant Flight Path in units of the atomic radius, Rat.
whatsThis: Used when the flight path sampling algorithm is set to Constant, flight_path_type=Constant.

fields.name: max_rel_eloss
fields.label: Max (ΔE/E)e
fields.toolTip: Maximum allowed relative electronic energy loss per flight path.
whatsThis: If this value is exceeded in a given flight path Δs, then Δs is truncated so that the ion suffers the maximum allowed relative energy loss and no collision takes place.
Applicable only when flight_path_type=Variable.

fields.name: min_recoil_energy
fields.label: Min recoil E (eV)
fields.toolTip: Minimum recoil energy in eV.
whatsThis: Recoils with energy below this value will be ignored if the scattering angle is also below min_scattering_angle.
Applicable only when flight_path_type=Variable.

fields.name: min_scattering_angle
fields.label: Min θ (º)
fields.toolTip: Minimum scattering angle θ in degrees.
whatsThis: Refers to the projectile scattering angle in the lab reference frame.
Events with scattering angle lower than this value will be ignored if the recoil energy is also below min_recoil_energy.
Applicable only when flight_path_type=Variable.

fields.name: mfp_range
fields.label: Ion mean free path range (Rat)
fields.toolTip: Defines the lower and upper limit of the ion mean free path in units of the atomic radius, Rat.
whatsThis: The lower limit is typically set equal to 1 Rat. This is equivalent to a cutoff radius Rc for the potential, V(R>Rc)=0, where Rc~Rat.
Setting the lower limit below 1 Rat increases Rc and allows scattering by distant atoms.
The upper limit can be useful for the simulation of light atoms in thin targets, where the mfp can become much larger than the target thickness.
Applicable only when flight_path_type=Variable.

fields.name: type

valueDescriptions: All ions have the same energy

Ion energy distributed according to the Gaussian (Normal) distribution around the center value with given fwhm

fields.whatsThis: When sampling from a distribution, out-of-bounds values are rejected and a new sample is drawn.

fields.name: center
fields.label: Central energy (eV)
fields.toolTip: Center (mean) of the generated ion energy distribution in eV.

fields.name: fwhm
fields.label: FWHM (eV)
fields.toolTip: Full-width at half-maximum of the generated ions energy distribution in eV.

fields.name: spatial_distribution
fields.label: Spatial Distribution
fields.toolTip: Definition of the generated ions spatial distribution.

fields.name: geometry
fields.label: Source geometry
valueDescriptions: Ions are generated on the left yz-plane bounding the simulation volume.
Ions are generated within the simulation volume.
fields.toolTip: Geometry of the ion source.

fields.name: type
fields.label: Distribution type
valueDescriptions: All ions have the same initial position
Ion position distributed uniformly around the center position
Ion position distributed according to the Gaussian (Normal) distribution around the center position with given fwhm
fields.toolTip: Type of spatial distribution of the generated ions.
whatsThis: Surface (2D) distributions are sampled on the left yz-plane bounding the simulation box.
In a Uniform surface (volume) distribution, the position is sampled uniformly in a square (cube) of width fwhm around the center.
In a Gaussian distribution, each component of the position vector is sampled from a Gaussian with the same fwhm around the center.
When sampling from a distribution, out-of-bounds positions are rejected and a new sample is drawn.

fields.name: center
fields.label: Center position (nm)
fields.toolTip: Center (mean) of the generated ions position distribution, [x,y,z] in nm.
fields.whatsThis: Must be either within the simulation box or at the lowest yz-plane boundary.

fields.name: fwhm
fields.label: FWHM (nm)
fields.toolTip: Full-width at half-maximum of the generated ions position distribution in nm.

fields.name: angular_distribution
fields.label: Angular Distribution
fields.toolTip: Definition of the generated ions angular distribution.

fields.name: type
fields.label: Distribution type
valueDescriptions: All ions have the same initial direction
Ion direction distributed uniformly within a cone around the central direction
Ion direction distributed according to a 2D isotropic Gaussian around the central direction
fields.toolTip: Type of angular distribution of the generated ions.
whatsThis: For the Gaussian distribution the transverse direction components tx,ty ~ N(0,sigma). Polar angle θ follows the Rayleigh distribution, azimuthal angle φ is automatically uniform.

fields.name: center
fields.label: Center direction
fields.toolTip: Ion beam central direction vector, [nx,ny,nz], unnormalized.

fields.name: fwhm
fields.label: FWHM (srad)
fields.toolTip: Width in srad of a cone around the central ion beam direction.
whatsThis: For the Uniform distribution, fwhm defines a cone around the main direction, where the direction of generated ions is sampled uniformly
For the Gaussian distribution, fwhm defines the solid-angle width around the main direction, sampled via an isotropic 2D Gaussian in the transverse components

fields.name: coordinate_system
fields.label: Tally coordinate system
fields.toolTip: Local coordinate system used to interpret the tally's bin coordinates.
whatsThis: Ion positions and directions are transformed into the UserTally coordinate system before binning.
The local coordinate system is defined by the origin, a z-axis direction vector and a vector on the xz-plane.
The z-axis direction vector and the xz-plane vector must not be parallel.
With default values, the UserTally coordinate system is identical to the simulation coordinate system.

fields.name: origin
fields.label: Origin [x₀,y₀,z₀] (nm)
fields.toolTip: Origin of the UserTally coordinate system.
fields.whatsThis: The vector is defined in simulation coordinates.

fields.name: zaxis
fields.label: Z-axis direction vector
fields.toolTip: A vector parallel to the z-axis of the UserTally coordinate system.
whatsThis: zaxis must not be parallel to xzvector.
The vector is defined in simulation coordinates.

fields.name: xzvector
fields.label: Vector on the xz-plane
fields.toolTip: A vector on the xz-plane of the UserTally coordinate system.
whatsThis: xzvector must not be parallel to the zaxis.
The vector is defined in simulation coordinates.

fields.name: bins
fields.label: Bin edges
fields.toolTip: Bin edge definitions for each variable scored by the tally.
whatsThis: The bin edges define the binning intervals for each variable.
The number of bins is equal to the number of bin edges minus one. Thus, bin egdes must contain at least two values.
A score is assigned to the i-th bin if the variable value x ∈ [b[i], b[i+1]), where b[i] is the i-th bin edge.
If x is outside the range of the bin edges, it is not counted.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.
The edges of at least one binning variable must be defined.

fields.name: x
fields.label: x-coordinate bin edges [nm]
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion position x-coordinate.
whatsThis: Coordinates refer to the UserTally coordinate system.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: y
fields.label: y-coordinate bin edges [nm]
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion position y-coordinate.
whatsThis: Coordinates refer to the UserTally coordinate system.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: z
fields.label: z-coordinate bin edges [nm]
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion position z-coordinate.
whatsThis: Coordinates refer to the UserTally coordinate system.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: r
fields.label: Radial distance r [nm]
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion's r=√(x^2+y^2+z^2).
whatsThis: Coordinates refer to the UserTally coordinate system.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: rho
fields.label: Cylindrical radial distance ρ [nm]
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion's ρ=√(x^2+y^2).
whatsThis: Coordinates refer to the UserTally coordinate system.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: cosTheta
fields.label: Polar angle cosine cosθ
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion's position polar angle cosine, cosθ = z/r.
whatsThis: Coordinates refer to the UserTally coordinate system.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: nx
fields.label: x-axis direction cosine
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion's x-axis direction cosine.
whatsThis: Coordinates refer to the UserTally coordinate system.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: ny
fields.label: y-axis direction cosine
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion's y-axis direction cosine.
whatsThis: Coordinates refer to the UserTally coordinate system.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: nz
fields.label: z-axis direction cosine
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion's z-axis direction cosine.
whatsThis: Coordinates refer to the UserTally coordinate system.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: E
fields.label: Ion kinetic energy [eV]
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion's kinetic energy.
whatsThis: Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: Tdam
fields.label: Ion damage energy [eV]
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion's damage energy.
whatsThis: Tdam refers to the energy of the PKA dissipated to atomic displacements during the whole cascade.
This variable can be used only with events of type CascadeComplete.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: V
fields.label: Number of generated vacancies
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the number of generated vacancies.
whatsThis: It refers to the total number of vacancies generated in a PKA cascade.
This can be used only with events of type CascadeComplete.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: atom_id
fields.label: Atomic species id
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion's atomic species id.
whatsThis: Each atomic species in the simulation is assigned an integer numeric id.
Beam ions always have an id of 0. Target atoms are given consequtive ids with id>=1.

If we have a target with 2 atomic species, the atomic ids will be 0, 1 and 2. With tally bin edges [0, 1, 2, 3], the first bin will count contributions from beam ions, the second bin will count target atoms of species 1 and the third bin will count target atoms of species 2.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.

fields.name: recoil_id
fields.label: Recoil generation id
fields.toolTip: Bin edges for the ion's recoil generation id.
whatsThis: Beam ions always have a recoil generation id of 0. Primary recoils (PKAs) have id=1. Higher-order recoils have id>1.
With bin edges [0, 1, 2], the first bin will count contributions from beam ions and the second bin will count contributions from PKAs.
Bin edges must be monotonously increasing.
